title: Monitor stack IaC assembly and health check orchestration
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and orchestration pattern to deploy and upgrade the full observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana + OpenTelemetry Collector + log shipping) into customer VPC/private clusters. Deliverables: module with clear inputs/outputs, idempotent upgrade hooks, automated preflight health checks, a canary rollout path, and runbooks for backups and rollback. Goal is to reduce manual upgrade work, improve upgrade safety for Private deployment customers, and expose health gates for the Redwood Private control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module `redwood.monitor_stack` published to internal registry and versioned
Automated pre-upgrade plan validation and a preflight script that verifies scrape targets, OTEL collector readiness, and log shipper queue depths
Canary rollout: ability to upgrade a single cell/cluster and promote on success
Healthcheck endpoints and SLOs documented and wired into console alerts
Runbook for Grafana dashboard backup + restore included
changes: Initial Terraform module scaffold: modules/prometheus, modules/grafana, modules/otel, modules/logship (2026-02-26)
Added Helm provider abstraction to support both EKS and on-prem K8s via `kubernetes` provider interpolation (2026-03-02)
Implemented a `preflight` null_resource with local-exec scripts that run synthetic checks (scrape /metrics, HTTP readiness for collector, disk/queue check for logship) (2026-03-05)
Wire in module outputs for health endpoints so Console can subscribe and create per-customer alerts (2026-03-10)
decisions: Use Helm charts managed via Terraform rather than raw manifests — reduces drift and simplifies upgrades (trade-off: depends on Helm provider stability)
Prefer in-place upgrades with health-driven rollbacks instead of blue/green for stateful components (Grafana) to avoid data duplication and long sync times
Expose a small set of module booleans to let customers opt-out of components (e.g., grafana_enabled=false) to keep module flexible
Keep Prometheus data retention unchanged during minor patch upgrades; provide an explicit migration path for retention/schema changes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Helm provider provider failures during mass upgrades. Mitigation: preflight provider version pin, and pre-check provider connectivity in CI pipeline
Risk: Grafana dashboard loss on accidental replacement. Mitigation: automatic dashboard export step before any change and store in S3 with versioned keys
Risk: OTEL Collector config change introducing high CPU. Mitigation: canary OTEL deployment to single cell and CPU limits + monitoring with rollback automation
Risk: Log shipper backlog growth during upgrade. Mitigation: preflight queue depth check and traffic shaping/pausing during canary window
test_plan: Unit: terraform fmt & validate for all modules and example manifests (CI)
Integration: apply to a disposable dev VPC and run synthetic probes against Prometheus, Grafana, OTEL, and logship
Chaos: simulate Helm chart failure to verify rollbacks and operator reconciliation
Load: generate scrape and log traffic to confirm autoscaling and queue behavior under upgrade paths
rollout_plan: 1) Publish module v1.0.0 to internal registry and update example/README
2) Dry-run in internal staging VPC using `terraform plan` and run preflight checks via CI job
3) Execute canary upgrade on single customer cell during maintenance window (2-hour window) — monitor health checks continuously
4) If canary passes for 30 minutes with no regressions, promote to 25% of cells, then 100% with automated spacing between waves
5) Automated rollback if any health gate fails; rollback implemented by `terraform apply` to previous module version and restore Grafana dashboards from backup
